newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks surge in foreign fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks surge in foreign fund buying.

text.p: Jordan's bourse surged to three-month highs on Tuesday sparked by the heaviest sustained demand from emerging funds seen in the last few years on select blue-chip mining and cement stock, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose another 0.57 percent to 157.62 points in healthy trade worth 1,524,345 dinars.

"Foreign buyers are being advised by local and international brokers of several potential GDRs (Global Depository Receipts) that could materialise before year-end," said Omar Masri, head of Amman-based Atlas Investment Group which deals with foreign funds.
"On this basis they are positioning themselves in those particular stock ahead of a potential rally," Masri said.
The market appears to be propelled by foreign buying, estimated to account for at least 70 percent of overall daily value since funds began stepping up their purchases last week.
Brokers estimate around $10 million worth of foreign buying in mainly three stock, Jordan Cement, Arab Potash and Jordan Phosphate Mines over the last two weeks alone.
The three firms, potential GDR candidates, have been focus of sustained foreign buying after the government passed a radically revised Jordan's companies law to encourage corporate capitalisation.
"We are witnessing concentrated buying on three out of 104 listed firms," Masri added.
But the lion's share of buying has been on Jordan Cement. The government plans to sell its 33 percent stake in the company in a possible GDR listing soon, investors said.
Jordan Cement again dominated volume with its 256,743 dinars worth of trade followed by small deals in Arab Potash Co and Jordan National Bank.

Brokers cite a bullish sentiment ever since the new laws were passed earlier this month. They were widely applauded by investors as evidence of government seriousness in accelerating moves to open the economy to foreigners.

Investment analysts say Jordan, which had lagged behind regional competitors, was now gaining more attention from emerging funds as it turned from one of the most expensive to the cheapest markets in the region.
The market is now seen as undervalued compared with other regional markets such as Egypt which have seen record inflows.
Brokers have cited some larger banks such as Housing Bank who own large holdings of blue-chips involved in some sales to outside funds.

But sustained availability of stock, in a market which suffers from a limited free float of blue chip shares, now hinges on prices rising higher to lure large institutions into profit-taking on their stock holdings.
"It's the foreign buying on some shares which is raising the share prices," said Abdul Mutaleb Abu-Hijleh general manager of Universal Investments Company brokerage firm.
Jordan Cement rose 0.02 dinars to 4.01 dinars for the fifth consecutive day. It was followed by a healthy 204,318 dinars worth of trade in Arab Potash which rose 0.03 dinars to 6.59 dinars.
Jordan National Bank rose 0.09 dinars to 1.96 dinars in moderate trade worth 161,362 dinars.
Overall advancing shares outnumbered losers by 21 to 10 while 14 were unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.10 percent to 79.79 points, 4.32 percent down from the start of the year.
